grammar_points.name: 〜でいて (please be/stay)

explanation.en:
How it works: Use で (de, state marker) + いて (ite, te-form of いる, 'to be') to request someone to remain in a certain state — 'please stay/be [adjective]'. Often used with adjectives and な-adjectives.

Example from this song: The song asks someone to stay a certain way — 'please remain as you are' — using でいて to express the wish for continued existence in that state.

More examples:
• 元気 (genki, 'healthy') → 元気でいて (genki de ite, 'please stay healthy')
• そのまま (sono mama, 'as is') → そのままでいて (sono mama de ite, 'please stay as you are')
• 優しい (yasashii, 'kind') → 優しくいて (yasashiku ite, 'please stay kind')

Note: For な-adjectives and nouns, use で: 元気でいて. For い-adjectives, use the く-form: 優しくいて. Adding ください makes it more polite: 元気でいてください.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 元気 (genki, 'healthy') + で (de, state) + いて (ite, 'be') → 元気でいて (genki de ite, 'please stay healthy')

grammar_points.name: 〜てしまう (end up doing, regrettably)

explanation.en:
How it works: Add てしまう (te shimau) after the te-form of a verb to express that something happened completely, often with regret or that it was unintentional. In casual speech, it contracts to ちゃう (chau) or じゃう (jau).

Example from this song: 忘れちゃう (wasurechau) = 'end up forgetting (regrettably)' — from 忘れる (wasureru, 'to forget') → 忘れて (wasurete, te-form) + しまう (shimau) → casual: 忘れちゃう (wasurechau)

More examples:
• 食べる (taberu, 'to eat') → 食べてしまう (tabete shimau, 'end up eating it all') → 食べちゃう (tabechau)
• 壊す (kowasu, 'to break') → 壊してしまう (kowashite shimau, 'accidentally break') → 壊しちゃう (kowashichau)
• 飲む (nomu, 'to drink') → 飲んでしまう (nonde shimau) → 飲んじゃう (nonjau)

Note: Contraction rules: てしまう → ちゃう, でしまう → じゃう. Past tense: ちゃった/じゃった. てしまう can also express completion without regret in some contexts.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 忘れる (wasureru, 'to forget') → 忘れて (wasurete) + しまう (shimau) → 忘れてしまう (wasurete shimau, 'end up forgetting') → 忘れちゃう (wasurechau, casual)

grammar_points.name: 〜たくなる (come to want to)

explanation.en:
How it works: Take the たい (tai, 'want to') form of a verb, change い to く, then add なる (naru, 'to become'). This expresses a spontaneous feeling arising — 'come to want to do X'.

Example from this song: 泣きたくなる (nakitaku naru) = 'come to want to cry' — from 泣く (naku, 'to cry') → 泣きたい (nakitai, 'want to cry') → 泣きたく (nakitaku) + なる (naru, 'become') = 泣きたくなる (nakitaku naru)

More examples:
• 食べる (taberu, 'to eat') → 食べたくなる (tabetaku naru, 'come to want to eat')
• 帰る (kaeru, 'to return') → 帰りたくなる (kaeritaku naru, 'come to want to go home')
• 会う (au, 'to meet') → 会いたくなる (aitaku naru, 'come to want to see someone')

Note: This describes feelings that arise naturally, not deliberate decisions. たい conjugates like an い-adjective: たい → たく (adverb form) + なる.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 泣く (naku, 'to cry') → 泣きたい (nakitai, 'want to cry') → 泣きたく (nakitaku) + なる (naru, 'become') → 泣きたくなる (nakitaku naru, 'come to want to cry')

grammar_points.name: 〜なくても (even without doing)

explanation.en:
How it works: Take the negative form of a verb (ない), change it to なくて (nakute), then add も (mo, 'even'). This means 'even if you don't do X' or 'even without doing X'.

Example from this song: 見回さなくても (miwasanakutemo) = 'even without looking around' — from 見回す (miwasu, 'to look around') → 見回さない (miwasanai, 'don't look around') → 見回さなくても (miwasanakutemo, 'even without looking around')

More examples:
• 言う (iu, 'to say') → 言わなくても (iwanakutemo, 'even without saying')
• 食べる (taberu, 'to eat') → 食べなくても (tabenakutemo, 'even without eating')
• 心配する (shinpai suru, 'to worry') → 心配しなくても (shinpai shinakutemo, 'even without worrying')

Note: なくても often implies 'it's fine / it'll be okay even without doing X'. Compare with なくてもいい (nakutemo ii, 'it's okay not to').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 見回す (miwasu, 'to look around') → 見回さない (miwasanai, 'don't look around') → 見回さなくても (miwasanakutemo, 'even without looking around')

explanation.en:
How it works: Change the verb ending to create a direct command. For -u verbs (godan), change the final syllable to its え-row equivalent. For -ru verbs (ichidan), replace る with ろ.

Example from this song: 歌え (utae) = 'Sing!' — from 歌う (utau, 'to sing') → change う (u) to え (e) = 歌え (utae)

More examples:
• 走る (hashiru, 'to run') → 走れ (hashire, 'Run!')
• 起きる (okiru, 'to wake up') → 起きろ (okiro, 'Wake up!')
• 頑張る (ganbaru, 'to do your best') → 頑張れ (ganbare, 'Do your best!')

Note: The imperative is very forceful. In this song, it's used as encouragement — 歌え means 'Sing!' in an inspiring way. Godan: う→え. Ichidan: る→ろ. The special verbs: する→しろ, 来る→来い (koi).

grammar_points.name: 〜んだよ (explanatory emphasis)

explanation.en:
How it works: Add んだよ (nda yo) at the end of a sentence to strongly explain or emphasize something. ん (n) is the contracted explanatory の (no), だ (da) is the copula, and よ (yo) adds assertive emphasis.

Example from this song: The song uses んだよ to assert emotional truths with feeling — 'that's the way it is!' or 'I'm telling you that...'.

More examples:
• 好き (suki, 'like') → 好きなんだよ (suki nandayo, 'I'm telling you, I like it!')
• 行く (iku, 'to go') → 行くんだよ (iku ndayo, 'I'm going, you know!')
• 大丈夫 (daijoubu, 'fine') → 大丈夫なんだよ (daijoubu nandayo, 'I'm telling you, it's fine!')

Note: んだよ is casual and direct. It's warmer than plain よ because の/ん adds the feeling of 'let me explain why'. After な-adjectives and nouns, add な before んだよ.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 好き (suki, 'like') + なんだよ (nandayo, 'I'm telling you') → 好きなんだよ (suki nandayo, 'I'm telling you, I like it!')
